expl: On 7–8 August 1942, a special meeting of the All India Congress Committee was held at the historic Gowalia Tank (August Kranti Maidan) in Bombay, in which the Wardha Resolution (Quit India) was ratified. After minor amendments, the resolution was adopted on 8 August 1942, and the formal launch of the Quit India Movement against the British, as part of India’s freedom struggle, took place on 8 August 1942 itself. On 9 August 1942, due to the arrest of leaders, the movement spontaneously spread among the masses. Thus, the practical beginning of the Quit India Movement is considered to be 9 August 1942. As soon as the movement began, under “Operation Zero Hour”, Gandhiji and other prominent Congress leaders were arrested. Gandhiji was arrested and kept in the Aga Khan Palace at Poona (Pune) along with Sarojini Naidu. The 1942 movement had the maximum impact in Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, the United Provinces and Madras.

stem: "We shall either free India or die in the attempt "who said it?
expl: This statement was made by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 on the occasion of the Quit India Movement. In the session of the All India Congress Committee at the Gowalia Tank ground in Bombay (now Mumbai)—later known as “August Kranti Maidan”—Gandhiji gave this message in the form of his famous slogan “Do or Die”. In his speech, he said that Indians must now resolve that either they will make India free, or they will sacrifice their lives in this effort.

stem: Quit India Movement was led by :
expl: The meeting of the All-India Congress Committee ended around midnight on 8 August, 1942. On 9 August, 1942, the police arrested major Congress leaders such as Mahatma Gandhi and Maulana Azad. Therefore, the movement became leaderless.

stem: The slogan ‘Do or Die’ was related with –
expl: The slogan mentioned in the question is associated with the Quit India Movement. On 8 August, 1942, the Quit India Resolution was passed after certain amendments. During this time, Gandhi’s statement was especially important: “I will not be satisfied with anything less than complete freedom. The British government may offer to abolish the salt tax, liquor-drinking, etc., but my words will be—nothing less than freedom. I give you a mantra—‘Do or Die’. Which area was affected most with the communal riots due to ‘Quit India’ Movement?
(i) Bihar (ii) Bengal
(iii) Gujarat (iv) United Province
Select your answer from the following code –
expl: The riots arising from the Quit India Movement (1942) were most widespread in Bihar and U.P. (United Provinces). An atmosphere like a rebellion developed there. In eastern U.P., Azamgarh, Ballia and Gorakhpur, and in Bihar, Gaya, Bhagalpur, Saran, Purnia, Shahabad, Muzaffarpur and Champaran became the main centres of spontaneous mass uprising.

stem: All India Azad Dasta at Bakri ka Tapu was organised during the Quit India Movement by:

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: During the Quit India Movement, Jayaprakash Narayan formed the “All-India Azad Squad” on an island called “Bakri ka Tapu”, located in the Terai region of Nepal, in the floodplain of the Kosi River. It was formed especially to carry out acts of sabotage against the government, so that the government’s war activities could be obstructed. In May 1943, under British pressure, the Government of Nepal arrested Jayaprakash Narayan. Those arrested along with him included Ram Manohar Lohia, Shyamnandan Singh, Vaidyanath Jha, and Kartik Prasad Singh.

stem: During the Quit India Movement parallel ‘National Government’ was established at many places. Which of the following is not correctly matched ?
expl: During the Quit India Movement, parallel governments were set up at various places— Prati Sarkar — Satara (Maharashtra) — Prati Sarkar was established in Satara (Maharashtra) under the leadership of Nana Patil. Praja Mandal — Talchhad (Talcher/Talcher) (Odisha) — In Talcher (Odisha), the Praja Mandal movement revolted against British rule and local rulers; it was a part of the Quit India Movement. Jatiya Sarkar — Tamluk (Bengal) — In Tamluk (Bengal), Jatiya Sarkar was established, which was a strong parallel government during the Quit India Movement. It handled many functions of local administration and continued the struggle against British rule. Raiyati Sarkar — The Raiyati Government was not established in Kheda; rather, it was established in Bardoli (Gujarat). The Raiyati Government was a parallel government set up during the Quit India Movement.
